newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO's Arafat says woman suicide bomber detained.
newsitem.headline: PLO's Arafat says woman suicide bomber detained.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said in remarks published on Monday his security forces detained a woman last week on her way to carry out a suicide bombing in Israel.
"Last Thursday, we detained a young Palestinian woman poised to carry out a suicide attack in Israel," The Israeli Maariv newspaper quoting Arafat as saying in an interview.

"She left a will with her parents where she wrote: 'Forgive me for what I did'. We immediately launched a search and, thank God, we succeeded in catching her before she managed to carry out her plan," he said.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu charges that Arafat is not doing enough to crack down on Hamas and Islamic Jihad, the two main militant Islamic groups opposing Israeli-PLO peacemaking.
The two groups have killed scores of Israelis in suicide attacks inside the Jewish state. Three Israeli women were killed in the last bombing at a Tel Aviv cafe in March.
Israeli troops arrested three Hamas activists near Nablus in a pre-dawn sweep on Monday, Palestinians said. They gave no more details.
The bombing followed Israel's groundbreaking on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem which deadlocked peacemaking with the PLO.
Arafat, who views Israeli settlement building as a violation of peace accords, warned of regional turmoil if the three-month impasse with Israel is not resolved.
"The whole area will slide into turmoil, I'm telling you the whole area. Not only between ourselves and the Israelis, but in the whole Middle East," he told the newspaper.

Another Israeli newspaper quoted U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright as telling an Israeli official that while Arafat had recently done "several stupid things", there was no alternative to his leadership.

Yedioth Ahronoth published excerpts of what it described as a top secret memo Israel's ambassador to the United States, Eliyahu Ben-Ellisar, sent his bosses in Jerusalem after meeting Secretary Albright two weeks ago.
It quotes Albright as saying at the meeting:
"I'm the last person to defend Arafat. He has recently done several stupid things which should not be done. But what's the alternative?...The alternative could be more extreme."
The foreign ministry said it was checking the report.
The United States has criticised Arafat's administration for reviving an old Jordanian law that imposes the death penalty against Arabs convicted of selling land to Jews.

Israel and the PLO signed an historic 1993 interim accord after decades of enmity but the suicide bombings, Israeli elections last year that swept the right-wing Netanyahu to power and Israeli settlement building have impeded peacemaking.
The deadlock in peace talks has been punctuated by clashes in the West Bank and Gaza in which Israeli troops have wounded scores of Palestinian protestors.
